Archer.name: Archer
Archer.description: Archers are highly specialized ranged combatants, who devote themselves to mastering the use of the bow. These masters of wood and steel are able to utilize a broad arsenal of ranged attacks. Archers are capable of mortally sniping from afar, penetrating the strongest armor, debilitating moving enemies, and even imbue their arrows with elemental energies. Adventuring parties are smart to employ the specialized, but highly capable combatants. This is good, as all but the most highly skilled Archer may, at times, find it difficult to adventure alone. Archers typically wear leather armor and can wield all ranged weapons and most melee weaponry. All Archers start with the class specific trait of High Ground, which increases your damage dealt with a bow when above your target, approximate 5%. A ranged based damage class, possessing situational abilities.

Bard.name: Bard
Bard.description: Bards are traveling musicians who learn to manifest song as a form of magic. Unlike the other great magic users of Eth-ur, who focus in a specific field, bardic magic is very diverse in its origins and capabilities. While a Bard’s song may not be as strong as certain magical spells, the experienced minstrel can bring to bear a solution for nearly any problem. Within an adventuring party a Bard is often sought out for their ability to enhance and inspire any allies. The time spent in taverns makes most Bards decent melee combatants, and quite capable of other roguish skills. When adventuring alone a clever Bard can find success in leveraging their wide range of skills and songs. Bards are capable of wielding nearly all weapons, instruments, and alcohol filled flagons, as well as wearing most types of armor.
Bard.bonus_advice: Listed below is the recommended allocation of bonus points by race. Since Charisma is a Bard’s main attribute, you should focus on maximizing it whenever possible. Most of your songs' effectiveness are tied to it. The remaining points are flexible, dexterity is supposed to be tied to missed notes but it is unknown how large of an effect this has. Because bards are often pulling for a group many players will opt to put their remaining points into stamina instead so that they can survive long enough to get back within range of the healer should problems arise. * Note: Mana total for a bard is now tied to charisma instead of int or wis like other classes. Dwarf: +7 Charisma, 3 flex points Halfling: +7 Charisma, 3 flex points Human: +6 Charisma, 4 flex points Wood Elf: +7 Charisma, 3 flex points

Beastmaster.description: Archetype: Animal-Taming Primal Brawler ; Roles: Melee DPS, Pet ; Races: Deep Gnome, Goblin, Halfling, Human, Ogre, Troll, Wood Elf ; The Beastmaster is a leather-armored melee brawler who fights without magic, instead choosing to have a bonded beast at their side. Where other classes channel supernatural forces, the Beastmaster draws on something rawer: physical power and a deep connection to the animal world. One animal fights alongside them as a persistent combat partner, while others aid them through their toolkit of bestial abilities. The Beastmaster is capable of strengthening both themselves and their companion, emphasizing the bond they share and their reliance on one another. Animal-inspired stances shift how the Beastmaster fights, but they aren’t magical; they evoke the instincts of someone who’s spent so much of their life living among animals that they’ve started to become one. Pets Pets are obtained with Bestial Bond, level through experience, and must be fed according to their diet. Store and swap them at a Kennel Master. From level 50, Call of the Faithful lets you summon a stowed pet from a distance. Swarm pets were removed; Kinship abilities provide temporary situational companions instead. Cleric.name: Cleric
Cleric.description: Clerics are those who devote their lives to mastering healing and protective powers stemming from their stalwart beliefs and discipline. This is most commonly, but not always, manifested through their faith in and service to a deity. Clerics are primarily magic users who specialize in the mending of wounds, curing ailments, and empowering their allies. Powerful Clerics may even bring their fallen allies back to life. Though Clerics excel at healing, they are competent melee combatants. Through strength of arm and unwavering faith, Clerics may smite their enemies with steel or employ powerful words and wards. Within an adventuring party a Cleric’s primary role is most often that of a healer, yet they can be fairly sturdy folk, and may take blows in place of their allies if the need arises. A Cleric may find difficulty adventuring alone, unless they are fighting foes which their faith specializes in the destruction of. ; ; Clerics prefer blunt weaponry and are typically seen in heavy plate armor.

Finally, put a point into Dexterity if you have any left. It affects hit rate across the board and increases your proc chance. Druid.name: Druid
Druid.description: Druids are protectors of the natural balance of Eth-ur. They are primarily spellcasters. Druids are adept healers, skillful augmenters, and competent wielders of nature’s destructive powers. Druidic magic on Eth-ur primarily employs elements from nature, but may harness astral powers as well. Offensively, these powers reflect nature’s most destructive elements. Situationally, the Druid truly shines: they may also erode a foe’s resistances to spells, provide various magical enhancements to allies, summon the aid of natural beings, and even harness their connection to other planes to facilitate teleportation. A Druid’s diverse capabilities allow them to fulfill many different roles amongst adventuring parties. And through clever use of their magic, they are often seen braving the wilds of Eth-ur alone. ; ; Long ago wood elven druids learned to see into the veins between the planes known as the wyrding. By traveling through druid rings or wyrd gates druids can move through the wyrding to teleport between locations1. ; ; Druids prefer to wear leather armor while wielding blunt weaponry or specialized blades, such as sickles and scimitars. ; ; 1: https://youtu.be/YOnTUusgDnE?t=2844

Finally, put a point into Dexterity if you have any left. It affects hit rate across the board and increases your proc chance. Elementalist.name: Elementalist
Elementalist.description: Elementalists are dedicated magic users who devote themselves to the study and mastery of elemental forces both on Eth-ur, and throughout the greater planes. An Elementalist is rarely without an elemental companion, and much of their magical ability is devoted to empowering or otherwise utilizing these companions in different ways. That being said, an Elementalist’s magic is very capable raining chaos and maelstrom upon their enemies directly. As a result of their interest and study of the elemental planes, Elementalists have learned the ability to conjure various useful, though sometimes strange, items with a myriad of different uses. Within adventuring parties it is most often the role of an Elementalist and their elemental companions to bring as much harm to the group’s foes as possible. Though, with the aid of their elemental allies, an Elementalist never truly adventures alone. ; ; Elementalists may wear cloth armor and have limited access to melee weaponry, often preferring staves, wands, and daggers. ; ; *Water pet is a Wizard, has a mana regen aura (Fount of Mana; since Beta 0.29 this stacks with Primary Mana Regeneration buffs), cast a nuke on target, tied lowest HP *Fire pet is a Wizard, has a damage shield + spell haste aura, cast a nuke on target, tied lowest HP *Air pet is a Monk, aura granting a chance to strike your target twice on melee and ranged attacks, cast stun on target, Monk Round Kick, medium HP, highest DPS *Earth pet is a Fighter, has HP Buff aura, cast root on target, provoke, highest HP *Since Beta 0.29, all four pet types are unlocked by level 12, and summons gain a new rank every 16 levels; each rank summons a pet matching your level. Note that every summoning costs reagents specifically Crushed Malachite sold by the Elemental quartermaster
Elementalist.bonus_advice: Below is the recommended allocation of bonus points by race. Since Intelligence is a Elementalist’s main attribute, you should focus on maximizing it whenever possible. Your spell damage and mana total is directly tied to it. After that, prioritize Stamina. It gives you extra HP and a bit of stun resistance. Finally, put a point or two into Dexterity. It affects hit rate across the board and increases your proc chance. Enchanter.name: Enchanter
Enchanter.description: Enchanters are subtle spellcasters who focus their study on magic which affects the mind and manipulates the ephemeral. Above all else, the Enchanter specializes in control and subterfuge. An Enchanter’s spellbook is diverse and situational. It is here, in those unique situations that the application of their magics is most powerful. Their greatest strength in battle is their ability to assault the minds of their foes causing them harm, incapacitating them momentarily, or turning them against their allies. Enchanters are also capable of imbuing their allies' weapons with magical effects, causing them to inflict greater harm with their blows. An Enchanter is most at home when adventuring with others, and their role within adventuring parties is primarily that of one who controls the battlefield. Fighter.name: Fighter
Fighter.description: Fighters are those who strive to become masters of the multitude of arms and armor that one may find through their travels. They excel at being at the heart of combat, taking blows for their allies and striking back in kind. Fighters are found in nearly every culture one may encounter while travelling across the continent of Aêthoril. A unifying link between all Fighters is the courage to stand toe-to-toe with even the greatest monsters of Eth-ur. As such, their commanding presence in battle can control the flow of the chaos by directing attention onto themselves. Most often a Fighter’s equipment is chosen based on what situations they may find themselves in, meaning that veteran Fighters often aim to have a diverse arsenal at their disposal. However, in terms of weaponry, many Fighters prefer to enter combat with a weapon in each hand, should the situation allow. While adventuring a Fighter should find themselves most comfortable when in the company of others. The world of Eth-ur is a dangerous place, and skill in battle alone can only get you so far when adventuring by yourself. Besides, without a group of companions in tow, who will carry their ale? ; ; Fighters may wear all armor types and are capable of wielding all weapons.

Inquisitor.name: Inquisitor
Inquisitor.description: Inquisitors are brutally efficient melee combatants who, through use of magic and force of will, assault the minds of their opponents to dominate and control the battlefield. Inquisitors are often employed by various organizations throughout the continent of Aêthoril as enforcers of said employer’s particular brand of justice. Inquisitors tend to be driven folk who will get a job done no matter the cost - and in the most direct manner imaginable. Using their magical training, an Inquisitor is capable of quite a few different ways to assault an opponent’s mind. This includes, temporarily rendering a foe unconscious, eroding an opponent’s willpower making them more vulnerable to attack, and permanently damaging their psyche. Inquisitors often find themselves as the focus of their foe’s attention, making them well suited for the role of protector within adventuring parties. While adventuring alone, an Inquisitor may find some difficulty, though through skill and determination may still find some manner of success. ; ; Inquisitors may wear plate armor and wield most weapons.

Monk.name: Monk
Monk.description: Monks are skilled martial artists who devote themselves to shaping their bodies into deadly, yet graceful, instruments of violence. For many Monks this devotion is of a spiritual nature, though this is not necessarily true for all of them. Most Monks view battle as a grim necessity to further their art. Others view battle as a righteous and glorious end, rather than a means. Monks choose to face their opponents up close and head on. Above all else, Monks choose to master the use of their body as a weapon. With deadly blows, well placed kicks, artful dodging, and even the ability to fake their own death, Monks make for potent melee combatants. Within an adventuring group, Monk’s use their speed, dexterity, and bravery to draw in foes for their allies to fight. They also deal significant harm to their enemies, and if needed, maintain the attention of said enemies. Some Monks may find adventuring alone a difficult task. Others use their unique skills to help them through periods of solitude, while they wander Eth-ur, meeting people and finding new adventures. ; ; Monks may wear leather armor, and they prefer to fight with their fists or wield staves.

Necromancer.name: Necromancer
Necromancer.description: Necromancers are shadowy spellcasters who dedicate themselves to the study of the soul and it’s connection to life. Necromancers are most infamously known for their study of, and often reanimation of (or otherwise tampering with) corpses. Many people view Necromancers with disdain and distrust if, not outright revulsion, due to the grim (and some believe, profane) nature of their work. The pages of an experienced Necromancer’s grimoire contain many different curses which debilitate and harm, both the living and the undead. A Necromancer’s greatest tool however, is their ability to animate undead minions. They are also capable of shaping flesh and bone in order to mend wounds… though such magic often comes at a personal cost. While adventuring, a Necromancer’s purpose is to harm and debilitate their foes while their allies, be they undead servant or fellow adventurer, shield them from harm. A Necromancer can find success both within adventuring parties and while adventuring alone. ; ; Necromancers wear cloth armor and typically wield staves, wands, scythes, and daggers.
Necromancer.bonus_advice: Below is the recommended allocation of bonus points by race. Since Intelligence is a Necromancer’s main attribute, you should focus on maximizing it whenever possible. Your spell damage and mana total is directly tied to it. After that, prioritize Stamina. It gives you extra HP and a bit of stun resistance. Finally, put a point or two into Dexterity. It affects hit rate across the board and increases your proc chance. Gnome: +4 Stamina, +1 Dexterity, and +5 Intelligence Goblin: +3 Stamina, +1 Dexterity, and +6 Intelligence Human: +2 Stamina, +1 Dexterity, and +7 Intelligence

Ranger.name: Ranger
Ranger.description: Archetype: Wilderness Veteran ; Roles: Melee + Ranged DPS, Utility ; Races: Deep Elf, Dwarf, Goblin, Halfling, Human, Ogre, Wood Elf ; The Ranger is a chain-wearing martial class whose identity is rooted in the wild. Their skills have been honed by a lifetime spent living off the land, not by channeling nature as a magical force like the Druid. What seems like magic to others is accumulated fieldcraft: old wisdom, remembered paths, and skills refined through years of necessity. In combat, they move fluidly between bow and blade depending on what the situation demands, and are capable of holding the line in a pinch. Outside of combat, however, is where the Ranger's full value emerges. They’re masters of travel, moving themselves and their group across terrain with ease. Their affinity with the land runs deepest in outdoor zones, where they can track down what others would miss, move through dangerous territory unseen, and live off the land unabated. Between fights, practical knowledge replaces spells. Wounds are dressed, ailments treated, and downtime cut short through their fieldcraft. The Ranger's skills turn a simple camp into something more—the group recovers better, and the wilderness provides in ways it wouldn't for anyone else. ;

Rogue.name: Rogue
Rogue.description: Rogue’s are deft combatants who devote themselves to mastering the use of stealth, poisons, and all manner of tricks. All across the land of Aêthoril, wherever you find a shady back alley, a run down tavern, crowded marketplace, or gathering of distracted nobles… you'll also find Rogues. They are also known as skilled informants, thieves, and even assassins. Rogues bring a plethora of skills into combat. The use of poisons to harm or debilitate their foes. Or the use of a well placed strike may catch an opponent off guard, temporarily taking them out of the fight. In tough situations a skilled Rogue may quickly vanish from sight, allowing them a chance at a surprise attack or the option to leave the battle altogether. However, they are at their best when their foes are distracted by others, as to turn your back on a Rogue is to invite a pointed outcome. In adventuring parties a Rogue's role is that of melee combat, focusing on the destruction of their enemies. While adventuring alone they may find it hard to take down stronger enemies, but through stealth and the picking of pockets it’s feasible that they can at least afford a beer or two. ; ; Rogues prefer lighter armor, but can wield most melee weaponry. ; ; For assistance completing your rogue starter quest, see Rogue Initiation Quest, Rogue Starter Quest (Faelindral), or Rogue Start Quest (Underdocks).

Shadow Knight.description: Shadow Knights are grim combatants who commit their lives wholly towards seeking out the greatest evils lurking throughout Eth-ur, no matter the cost. Their motivations differ: some search the darkness for personal power or fame, while others carry with them a vendetta or bright mission wrapped in a black cloak. Shadow Knights harness magic that originates from the very darkness they strive so relentlessly to combat. This magic primarily takes the form of draining and leeching spells, as well as spells which shape shadows to enhance the caster’s defenses. Within adventuring parties it is often a Shadow Knight’s duty to attract the ire of their foes away from their allies, though they are also quite capable at inflicting harm. When adventuring alone a Shadow Knight may find some success through clever use of their magic. ; ; Shadow Knights are melee combatants who are able to make use of some magic. Shadow Knights usually prefer to wield two-handed weapons, though are capable of wielding all weapons.

Shaman.name: Shaman
Shaman.description: Shamans are animistic spellcasters who study and commune with spirits, souls, and nature. For many cultures across Aêthoril, and Eth-ur more broadly, Shamans serve as spiritual leaders and moral guides. Within these cultures the Shaman often takes on the role of mediator between ancestor spirits and descendants, allowing communication between the two parties. The Shaman often walks along the edge of many realities. Shamans are powerful healers with access to many regenerative spells. They also have access to a wide range of spells which may enhance an ally’s combat prowess or debilitate and destroy their enemies. Experienced Shamans may summon beastial spirits to aid them in combat. Though most powerful when casting spells, they are also capable melee combatants when the need arises. Within an adventuring party a Shaman most often takes on a supporting role. When adventuring alone they may find some success through clever use of their abilities. ; ; Shamans may wear chain armor as well as wield blunt and piercing weaponry.
Shaman.bonus_advice: Listed below is the recommended allocation of bonus points by race. Since Wisdom is a Shaman’s main attribute, you should focus on maximizing it whenever possible. Wisdom is directly tied to your healing spells effectiveness and total mana. After that, prioritize Stamina. It gives you extra HP and a bit of stun resistance. Finally, put a point into Dexterity if you have any left. It affects hit rate across the board and increases your proc chance. Goblin: +4 Stamina and +6 Wisdom Human: +2 Stamina, +1 Dexterity, and +7 Wisdom Ogre: +2 Dexterity and +8 Wisdom Wood Elf: +3 Stamina and +7 Wisdom

Wizard.name: Wizard
Wizard.description: Wizards are dedicated scholars of the magical arts. A Wizard seeks to become a master of magic through study and practice. As the forerunners of magical knowledge and resource, they hold the ability to cast the most complex and dangerous spells available to mortals. Wizards excel at bringing battles to a swift end from afar with correctly chosen and deliberately timed spells. Should they become too depleted to use their spells, they are able to enter melee, delivering magically enhanced blows that reinvigorate themselves. Wizards are also capable of making foes more vulnerable to magic, enhancing allies' blows with extra effects, and manipulating the fabric of reality with teleportation focused magic. Within adventuring parties a Wizard's role is focused on violence of action; to deal as much harm as possible, as quickly as possible. Some Wizards may find adventuring alone to be difficult, but clever use of spells could prove otherwise. ; ; Wizards may wear cloth armor as well as wield staves, swords, and daggers.
Wizard.bonus_advice: Below is the recommended allocation of bonus points by race. Since Intelligence is a Wizard’s main attribute, you should focus on maximizing it whenever possible. Your spell damage and mana total is directly tied to it. After that, prioritize Dexterity. It affects hit rate across the board and increases your proc chance. Finally, put some points into Stamina for extra HP and a bit of stun resistance. Dwarf: +1 Stamina, +2 Dexterity, and +7 Intelligence Gnome: +3 Stamina, +2 Dexterity, and +5 Intelligence Human: +1 Stamina, +2 Dexterity, and +7 Intelligence
